narrative_purpose: A label-ready vertical specimen plate shows the mismatch between light at the surface and regenerated nutrients at depth, connected downward by marine snow.
subject: A tall vertical cutaway through open ocean. The upper fifth is bright cyan water crowded with tiny translucent plankton cells beneath sunbeams. A narrow wavering density boundary separates it from darker blue water. Below, a sparse stream of organic flakes, pellets and cell fragments falls through the middle. Near the bottom, faint teal dissolved clouds suggest a deep nutrient reservoir without symbols or arrows.
scene: An isolated ocean column presented like a naturalist specimen, with no coastline and no seafloor machinery.
camera: Straight-on vertical section, surface at the top edge and deep water occupying most of the frame.
light: Bright diffuse cyan at the surface fading exponentially into indigo; marine-snow particles catch small teal highlights; the deep reservoir has only a faint internal glow.
palette: Mist and cyan surface, ocean teal transition, void-indigo depth, living-teal particles and a rare amber organic flake.
style: Painterly scientific specimen plate with soft organic textures, not a chart or vector infographic.
detail_level: Distinct surface cells, density boundary, falling particle types and dark deep water; uncluttered margins for annotations.
composition: Strong vertical gradient with four visually separable regions and a continuous falling particle path slightly right of center.
consistency_notes: The plate must communicate vertical separation through light, particle density and colour alone. No baked-in scientific notation.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no numbers, no chart axes, no flat infographic, no photographic or 3D-render look, no decorative fantasy storm
